conversation.content: Blitzen Trapper is an experimental country/folk/rock band from Portland, Oregon, associated with Sub Pop, Vagrant, Lojinx, and Yep Roc Records. Formed in 2000, the current lineup includes Eric Earley, Brian Adrian Koch, Michael Elson, and Nathan Vanderpool, with occasional support from Michael Blake. The band self-released their first three albums. Their third album, "Wild Mountain Nation," gained critical acclaim in 2007, leading to a deal with Sub Pop Records. In 2008, "Furr" received high praise from Rolling Stone, ranking No. 13 in the Best Albums of 2008. Subsequent albums include "Destroyer of the Void" and "American Goldwing." "VII" was released in 2013 on Vagrant Records, followed by "Live In Portland" and "Live Harvest." "All Across This Land" came out in 2015, and "Wild and Reckless" in 2017. After a lineup change in 2019, the band released "Holy Smokes Future Jokes" on Yep Roc in 2020 and resumed touring in 2022.

Metric is a Canadian indie rock band formed in 1998 in Toronto, consisting of Emily Haines, James Shaw, Joshua Winstead, and Joules Scott-Key. Initially named "Mainstream," the band changed to Metric after releasing the "Mainstream EP." 

Their debut album, "Old World Underground, Where Are You Now?" was released in 2003. Their second album, "Live It Out" (2005), received nominations for the Polaris Music Prize and Juno Awards. "Grow Up and Blow Away," recorded in 2001, was delayed and released in 2007.

Their subsequent albums include "Pagans in Vegas" (2015), "Art of Doubt" (2018), "Formentera" (2022), and "Formentera II" (2023). Metric ranked 41st on Rolling Stone's "The 50 Greatest Canadian Artists of All Time" in 2023.

conversation.content: I’m not convinced that passenger traffic trends post-health crises actually reflect genuine recovery—more often, they just mask temporary spikes driven by pent-up demand or promotional discounts, not sustainable behavioral shifts. Sure, airlines tout “record bookings,” but how many of those travelers are just rescheduling postponed trips rather than forming new habits? And let’s be honest, when a carrier offers 50% off transatlantic flights, you’re not seeing organic demand—you’re seeing desperation to fill seats. The real question isn’t whether people flew again—it’s whether they’ll keep flying once the deals dry up and fuel prices climb back. Plus, business travel hasn’t truly rebounded; remote work is still eating into corporate budgets, and hybrid models mean fewer frequent flyers. Are we measuring recovery or just noise from short-term incentives? True resilience would show in consistent leisure demand, not flash sales and loyalty point dumps. If traffic dips again next winter, will we admit the bounce was an illusion—or just blame another variant?

conversation.content: Otro Día Más Sin Verte (English: Just Another Day), also called Sentir in Spain, is the Spanish-language debut album by Cuban singer Jon Secada. It was released on October 6, 1992 by EMI Latin to coincide with his English-language self-titled debut album, which was released in April 1992. The idea to release an all Spanish-language album was pitched by Secada's music mentor Emilio Estefan, after realizing that SBK Records have yet released such an album. Estefan presented Secada's proposal for a Spanish-language recording to the head of Capitol EMI Records Charles Koppelman and then president of EMI Latin Jose Behar. Koppelman accepted the proposal after Behar stated that he could see "market potential" for Secada. With the help of Emilio's wife, Gloria Estefan, Secada translated selected compositions from his English-language debut album for Otro Día Más Sin Verte.
